children: Paramount Chief Executive David Ellison has picked HBO content chief Casey Bloys to oversee streaming operations once the company combines with Warner Bros. Discovery, people familiar with the matter said.
It's the first major executive decision by Ellison ahead of Paramount's planned $81 billion acquisition of Warner, which owns HBO and streaming service HBO Max.

As a result, Cindy Holland, the former Netflix programming executive whom Ellison put in charge of Paramount's streaming platforms including Paramount+ about a year ago, is leaving the company. In a memo to staff, Holland said Tuesday was her last day.

"As David readies for the next phase of his vision, we've discussed my role and the future of the combined businesses," Holland wrote. "David is optimizing for HBO stability as we move into this next chapter, and I fully support that."

The moves come as Paramount awaits a judge's approval of the settlement agreement it reached last week with 12 Democratic state attorneys general who had sought to block the Warner merger on antitrust grounds.

Ellison's decision to choose Bloys over Holland ends a Hollywood parlor game over who would land what is considered one of the most important roles at the combined company. Bloys is considered a premier programmer, while HBO has long been viewed as the gold standard among entertainment platforms.
Ellison was concerned that losing Bloys would damage the HBO brand, which is a crucial part of the company's streaming strategy, one of the people familiar with the matter said.
Bloys wasn't interested in partnering with another executive to run the streaming operation and had made that clear to Paramount, people familiar with his thinking said.
In a statement, Ellison praised Holland, saying she is a "force of nature whose impact on Paramount over the past year has been significant."
Holland didn't respond to a request for comment. The New York Times first reported news of her departure.

Holland was one of Ellison's first major appointments when his Skydance Media production company took control of Paramount in August 2025. She made several high-profile deals including wooing "Stranger Things" creators Matt and Ross Duffer to Paramount.
Conversely, Taylor Sheridan, the prolific creator of "Yellowstone," "Landman" and other hits, signed a deal to leave Paramount for NBCUniversal on her watch.
Holland also played a key role in Paramount's battle against Netflix to acquire Warner, people familiar with the matter said.

At Netflix, Holland was an architect of the original programming strategy that helped establish the streaming service as a global powerhouse with shows like "House of Cards" and "Orange is the New Black."
Bloys first joined HBO in 2004 and has headed programming since 2016. Shows developed during his tenure include "Succession," "Girls," "Veep" and "The White Lotus."
Additional shake-ups are expected in the days ahead once Paramount gets official court approval of the settlement, which could come as early as this week.
